newsitem.title: USA: Digital sees Q4 net, revs improving from Q3.
newsitem.headline: Digital sees Q4 net, revs improving from Q3.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp Chief Financial Officer Vincent Mullarkey said he expects improvements in revenues, earnings and gross margins and on its balance sheet in the fourth quarter from the third.

"Looking forward now to this quarter, the fourth quarter, expectations are that we will have a sequential revenue increase, comparable to what we've experienced over the last couple of years; a good solid continuation of gross margin improvement; profit improvement; and of course, continued balance sheet improvement," he told reporters on a telephone conference call.
When asked specifically about fourth quarter revenues, Mullarkey said he expected a "fairly significant improvement" over the third quarter.

Mullarkey said fluctuations in currencies cost the company, which derives more than half its revenues overseas, a little over $60 million in the third quarter. Fourth quarter earnings will be hit by a similiar amount or more, he added.

"We were impacted...by some $60 million, a little over that actually, in profit this quarter," he said. "The outlook for the fourth quarter is more of the same. The indicators would suggest it's going to be equal to or worse..." he said.
The company said at the beginning of the fiscal year it would purchase 10 million shares this year, and during the first three quarters, it bought back about six million shares.
Mullarkey said he expected Digital to complete the share repurchase program in the fourth quarter by buying back about four million shares.
"It is our intention to complete this phase of our repurchase activities this fiscal year," he said.
Mullarkey said unit sales of its Alpha-based computer systems rose in the third quarter over the second quarter, but revenues were hit by price cuts.
"Total Alpha systems revenues were down two percent versus quarter two, while Alpha unit sales were up six percent," he said.
He said the higher unit sales were not enough to offset the steep price cuts announced earlier this year in Alpha workstations and servers.

Digital Chief Executive Robert Palmer said he was happy with the performance of many of the company's businesses, including its microprocessor and Internet service provider units, but was disappointed with the dip in revenues.
Digital's revenues dropped to $3.3 billion in the third quarter from $3.6 billion the previous third quarter, including a fall in product sales to $1.8 billion from $2.1 billion.
"We cannot be satisfied with anything less than competitive levels of growth and profitability," he said. "I'm optimistic that in the next few quarters we can continue to grow again," he added.
